chunks: People rise from their beds in three categories: one for whom it is in their favor and not against them, one for whom it is against them and not in their favor, and one for whom it is neither against them nor in their favor.

As for the category that is in their favor and not against them, they rise from their sleep, perform wudu (ablution), pray, and remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That is the one for whom it is in their favor and not against them.
As for the second category, they remain in disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is the one for whom it is against them and not in their favor.
And as for the third category, they continue sleeping until morning; that is the one for whom it is neither against them nor in their favor.

key_terms.أَصْبَحَ: morning came; he reached the morning
key_terms.فُرُشِهِمْ: their beds, indicating the state from which people rise
key_terms.نَائِمًا: sleeping, without engaging in worship or sin

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام classify people who rise from sleep at night or in the morning?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام divides people at the time of rising from sleep into three categories based on how they respond spiritually. The one who rises for wudu (ablution), salat (prayer), and dhikr (remembrance of God) gains benefit, the one occupied in disobedience incurs loss, and the one who merely sleeps through until morning has neither gain nor burden. The hadith encourages wakefulness for worship, especially in the context of the night prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1365 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"People rise from their beds in three categories: one for whom it is in their favour and not against them, one for whom it is against them and not in their favour, and one for whom it is neither in their favour nor against them.

As for the one who is in their favour and not against them, they rise from their sleep, perform wudu (ablution), pray, and remember Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. This is the one for whom it is in their favour and not against them.
As for the second category, they remain engaged in disobedience to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic; this is the one for whom it is against them and not in their favour.
As for the third category, they continue sleeping until morning; this is the one for whom it is neither in their favour nor against them."
